Messages.Body:
This is mainly to tom . Yes I have made some mistakes in reading your
posts , but I'll admit when I'm wrong ( and have done ) . And yes i am
basing these comments on Errol's quoted texts so flame me if I am
foolish enough to use faulty information (but yes I trust you Errol).
Could you justify
Archon Investigation and JUsticar Retribution for me please . Your current
answers and analogies havent really been satisfactory . Your comparison of
gangrel aggro and AI conveniently neglected to mention that there are
methods to avoid the aggro when in combat with a gangrel , but there are no
ways to protect yourself when doing big bleeds (ok maybe aura reading or
owl companion to check the hands but this is difficult especially if you
are avoiding combat , and Pulse of the canaille costs 3 blood and an action) .
There needs to be a workable counter to this card .
Ok there is going to be new ideas in cards . Good . Of the 4 new cards
in Errol's post 2 appeared fair , while 2 were dodgy to say the least .
Please try not to anfairly advantage one of combat/bleed/vote in the
future , and also try,try,try to avoid the 1 cards kills a strategy
munchkinisation that seems to be starting .

JA Chapman .

ps - has anyone noticed on the new clan hosers that the clan symbol appears .
This has better be errata (it may already have been , sorry if i missed it) .
If it isnt doesnt it defeat the purpose of the hosers , which I interpret to
be to disadvantage people using vampires of a clan , usually other than your
own . How many tremere players would want to play Letter from Vienna ?.....

cmbat

In article <486uap$9...@harbinger.cc.monash.edu.au> jac...@aurora.cc.monash.edu.au (Mr JA Chapman) writes:

>[... Archon Investigation and JUsticar Retribution ...]

>in Errol's post 2 appeared fair , while 2 were dodgy to say the least .
> Please try not to anfairly advantage one of combat/bleed/vote in the
>future , and also try,try,try to avoid the 1 cards kills a strategy
>munchkinisation that seems to be starting .

I'm sorry, but it seems that those 2 cards do not need any justification.
Jyhad carries the Mt$ tradition, and inherits many of its aspects; it
is only expected that a card will hose bleeds as much as Karma hoses
Black. "1 card kills a strategy"? That is a /must/ in (almost, eh)
every CCG. A CCG is never the same without those. It is not just
`starting'; it has started, is deeply rooted in the CCG traditions,
and will be there to bug you for a long while.

Look at the 2 new Mt$ clones. How many cards in these "new" games
seem familiar? "Flight of Dragons" in [L5R] ... Swallow that,
Mr. Chapman; this is a TREND, set by the first, leading game.
It is assumed that if you put in lots of mega-hosers, they will
somehow balance themselves out, and if they don't, the game will
still be played and loved by the players anyway, as evident from
the big success of `the phenomenum'.

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Mr JA Chapman <jac...@aurora.cc.monash.edu.au> wrote:
>Could you justify
>Archon Investigation and JUsticar Retribution for me please . Your current
>answers and analogies havent really been satisfactory . Your comparison of
>gangrel aggro and AI conveniently neglected to mention that there are
>methods to avoid the aggro when in combat with a gangrel , but there are no
>ways to protect yourself when doing big bleeds (ok maybe aura reading or
>owl companion to check the hands but this is difficult especially if you
>are avoiding combat , and Pulse of the canaille costs 3 blood and an action) .

The basic idea behind Archon Investigation and Justicar Retribution is
to hose massive bleed decks, yes. But they do not hose bleeding in general:
you can still run effectively at 2-3 bleed per action.

>There needs to be a workable counter to this card .

Hosers for hosers is actually a ludicrous concept. Archon Investigation does
exactly what a hoser is supposed to do: it makes people think twice about
following the strategy it hoses. Yes, it would be nice if you could Suddenly
Reverse it... but this is true of most out-of-turn cards. No, it wouldn't be
as vicious if it required being bleed for 4... but the same would be true if
the card started at 5, 6, etc.

>ps - has anyone noticed on the new clan hosers that the clan symbol appears .
>This has better be errata (it may already have been , sorry if i missed it) .

It is errata, yes.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

But they already exist - S:CE is pretty much the ultimate combat hoser
but cards like psyche and hidden lurker exist that get around it .
You can also Sudden reverse many of the clan hosers..... And
its not the Malk decks that have the main problem , its the tap and bleeders .
The only really successful decks of these type that I have played against
have relied on getting through 1 bleed per round , and they have only
worked when this bleed has been substantial . Rephrase the card so it
can only be played 'immediately after a bleed of greater than 3 has been successful'. This way the player will have to pay a reasonable penalty for
playing it (ie taking a bleed as well as the 3 pool cost ) . The card will
still have a purpose - ie the big bleeders can only do it once - but the
controller of the bleeder will get at least some value for his effort . For
anyone with auspex the can still use telepathic counter to reduce the bleed
to 4 , and a total of 7 pool isnt really that much to pay to stop a pulsed/
laptopped vamp (especially a big one) cold . A really annoying use ive already
seen for this card is someone checking that their prey didnt have AI , then
the prey doing a deal with the bleeder's predator to bounce the bleed to them
and then the predator killed mariel - horrid and effective .
